To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) similarity to the self affects memory for impressions of other people, (2) this effect is dependent upon the valence of the impressions (positive or negative), (3) the effect of valence was found in both the high and medium self-similarity conditions.
the similarity of a target to the self affects how well that target's impression is remembered.
memory for others was better if the person was similar to the self and the impression was positive, but worse if the person was dissimilar to the self and impression was negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of similarity to the self on memory for impressions of other people.
understanding how similarity to the self affects memory for impressions of people.
the role of similarity to the self on memory for information about others.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
similarity to the Self AFFECTS memory for impressions of OTHERS.
the present studies provide evidence that similarity to the Self affects memory for impressions of Others.
people are better remembered when they have positive impressions of them and are similar to the self, but are less remembered when they have negative impressions of them and similar to the self.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people are better at remembering positive impressions of similar others and negative impressions of dissimilar others.
the self-reference effect is not limited to self-relevant information but also applies to impressions of others.
similarity to the Self affects memory for impressions of Others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people may be better at remembering others who are similar to themselves.
people remember others who are similar to themselves, especially when the impression is positive, but they forget others who are similar when the impression is negative.
similarity to the person is a critical factor in memory formation for people.
